verdict.summary: Synopsys is a high-quality design tollbooth undergoing a balance-sheet and accounting transition after Ansys. Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 42% to $2.477 billion; GAAP diluted EPS was $2.84 and non-GAAP EPS was $3.91, while management raised the full-year revenue midpoint to $9.715 billion and non-GAAP EPS midpoint to $15.07. AI reaches Synopsys before silicon ships: larger chips, chiplets, advanced packaging and physical-system validation expand electronic-design-automation runs, verification compute and licensable IP. The moat is real, but the captured 82.6% trailing gross margin masks a sharp GAAP/non-GAAP operating split: the company showed a 10.4% GAAP operating-margin midpoint against 41.5% non-GAAP after acquisition amortization, stock compensation and restructuring adjustments. Cash of $2.48 billion versus $10.84 billion debt makes Ansys integration central to equity quality. The 68/100 grade is therefore sensible, and distinct from timing. RSI 71.4 and a required close above $462.45 argue for confirmation, not pursuit. Wait: $462.45 is only a historical design reference. Synopsys needs a newly dated regular-session base before activation, sizing or any order can be considered.

business.overview:
Synopsys monetizes semiconductor and systems engineering through Design Automation software, Design IP and Ansys simulation assets. Revenue is driven by multi-year time-based licenses, maintenance, IP royalties and project timing rather than wafer shipments alone.

The AI transmission channel is design complexity: accelerators, custom silicon, chiplets, HBM interfaces and advanced packages require more verification, implementation, emulation, signoff and multiphysics simulation. That expands engineering spend even before a design reaches fabrication and gives Synopsys exposure to both merchant and custom AI silicon.

The model breaks if customers consolidate tools, internalize IP, delay tape-outs or resist pricing, and if Ansys integration disrupts selling or product roadmaps. Acquisition accounting and $10.84B of debt also mean revenue growth must translate into GAAP margin and cash, not only adjusted EPS. The pending Ansys integration adds simulation breadth but also debt, purchase-accounting noise and execution risk. Revenue recognition depends on term-license timing, renewals and IP milestones, so a strong quarter can coexist with volatile deferred revenue and cash conversion.
business.moat: Synopsys' moat comes from deeply qualified EDA workflows, foundry-certified process design kits, verification IP and file-format/toolchain dependencies accumulated over entire chip programs. Replacing a core signoff or verification tool creates schedule and silicon-re-spin risk; Ansys broadens the workflow into system simulation, but integration execution determines whether that breadth becomes cross-sell rather than complexity.

earnings.beatNote: Guidance/outlook is stated from the official release; Q3 FY2026 revenue was $2.477B versus $1.740B a year earlier, a 42% increase. GAAP net income was $545.8M and GAAP diluted EPS $2.84; non-GAAP net income was $752.5M and non-GAAP EPS $3.91. Management raised FY2026 revenue to a $9.715B midpoint and non-GAAP EPS to a $15.07 midpoint. The key caveat is the adjustment burden: at the midpoint, 10.4% GAAP operating margin reconciles to 41.5% non-GAAP after 16.6 points of acquired-intangible amortization, 9.8 points of stock compensation and other items. The investor release and SEC filing were source-checked through August 28, 2026; no confirmed next-earnings date was announced, so the dossier correctly reports next earnings as Not confirmed.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: Synopsys reported 191.605M shares outstanding at July 31, 2026. Q3 weighted-average shares were 191.536M basic and 192.319M diluted, a 0.783M treasury-method increment from equity compensation; another 1.523M employee awards were anti-dilutive and excluded. The 192.319M quarterly diluted average is the minimum observable denominator, not a point-in-time fully diluted count, which remains unavailable because unvested awards are not reconciled into one current total. The reviewed filings contain no ATM or equity sale. Capital risk instead sits in $10.84B Ansys-funded debt and recurring stock compensation.

filings.finding: The Q3 FY2026 Form 10-Q reports 191.605M shares outstanding and reconciles 191.536M basic weighted-average shares to 192.319M diluted through 0.783M equity-compensation equivalents; another 1.523M employee awards were anti-dilutive. It also supports the Ansys acquisition-accounting and debt baseline.

The August 26 Form 8-K furnishes the direct earnings exhibit showing $2.477B revenue, $2.84 GAAP EPS, $3.91 non-GAAP EPS and raised FY2026 revenue and non-GAAP EPS targets; it is not a financing filing.

The FY2025 Form 10-K provides the pre-Q3 business, customer, IP, competition and acquisition-risk baseline needed to distinguish durable EDA economics from Ansys purchase-accounting and integration effects.
